findings.text: §15's "own-session baseline on a first arm" exemption (`kind (None, state)`, delivered whenever the pane holds no checkpoint) is indistinguishable from the fleet baseline that `tests/test_follow_settled_rows.py::test_the_pane_receives_only_the_settled_changes` arms on: `_deliver` writes two own-session pointers at `phase="working"` (`test_follow_settled_rows.py:109,232`) with no prior stream content, so the first arming's `_fleet_replay` feeds two own-session baseline rows of kind `(None,"working")` — the same shape the exemption delivers — yet that test asserts `first == []` ("the attach's own re-announcements ask for nothing, so the first arming wakes nobody", line 256-258). Meanwhile the third negative control relies on the same exemption delivering the identical row shape in `test_follower_survives_a_config_change.py` (pointer `phase="working"`, line 169) and `test_follower_survives_a_host_change.py` (pointer `phase="working"`, line 57). One kind-keyed rule cannot both deliver and withhold it, so as written the exemption breaks the pin the done-when names.

findings.reason: a done-when that its own mechanism provably fails is the measurable form of the reasoning defect above; the plan must either narrow the exemption or move `test_follow_settled_rows.py` into the write paths and state how it is re-anchored.
